title: Excess Mileage Charge on Returned Closed-End Units (Kestrel Commercial Fleet Lease)
content:
# Lease-End Desk Guidance — Excess Mileage on Closed-End Commercial Units, Kestrel Commercial Fleet Lease

## Scope of the charge

For the excess mileage charge billed on a closed-end commercial unit of the Kestrel Commercial Fleet Lease whose lease ended by a turn-in or by a recovery after an uncured default, and only for that charge, the charge is figured as this policy states. A closed-end commercial unit ended by a purchase is billed excess mileage at the closed-end excess mileage rate for its vehicle class for miles above the annual mileage allowance multiplied by the months in service and divided by 12, as before, and this policy's figure does not apply to it. The wear charges of a closed-end unit are not part of this charge and remain under the master agreement's termination clause.

The turn-in date and turn-in odometer used for this charge are those the unit records for its turn-in or recovery.

| How the closed-end unit's lease ended | Excess mileage |
|---|---|
| Turn-in, at any point in the term | the excess mileage charge under this policy |
| Recovery after an uncured default | the excess mileage charge under this policy |
| Purchase | the class rate for miles above the annual allowance multiplied by the months in service and divided by 12, as before |

The charge falls due when a closed-end unit in the first two rows was driven beyond its allowance. What is booked is one unit charge of the type excess mileage charge on that unit; once billed, the unit's ledger carries that excess mileage charge and the unit's charges due balance includes it.

## System reference — `bill_excess_mileage_e7ed45ad`

**Capability.** Bills the excess mileage charge on a turned-in commercial fleet unit lease schedule: the servicing agent books one unit charge of the type excess mileage charge (`excess_mileage_charge`) on the named unit, dated today, in the amount given, and the unit's charges due balance rises by that amount. The business sees the excess mileage charge listed among the unit's billed charges and in its charges due.

**How it is invoked.** An agent-side tool: the servicing agent unlocks `bill_excess_mileage_e7ed45ad` and then calls it.

**Parameters.**

- `fleet_unit_id` — the reference number of the fleet unit lease schedule being billed, read from the fleet unit lookup for the business; an identifier.
- `amount` — the excess mileage charge in USD; a positive number with 2 decimal places (cents), already rounded to the cent, with no currency symbol.

**Return.** On success, a confirmation line naming the charge reference number (an opaque identifier for the new charge), the fleet unit reference number, the charge type `excess_mileage_charge`, the amount billed in USD with 2 decimal places, the billing date in YYYY-MM-DD form, and the unit's charges due balance in USD with 2 decimal places including this charge. A line beginning "Error:" means no unit matched the reference number and nothing was billed.

**Contract questions.**
- *Does the tool work out the amount?* No. It books the amount given.
- *What does the business see afterwards?* The excess mileage charge among the unit's billed charges and in its charges due.
